title: one LoRA to many virtual LoRAs
hypothesis: One rank-2 LoRA basis plus per-task rank-space Mirror rotations can recover multiple virtual adapter functions from one physical low-rank update at lower payload than independent LoRAs; generic shared-basis coefficient generation is the decisive control.
physical_object: shared LoRA factors A (16x2) and B (2x12)

task.task_address: oracle task id derived from signs of first three input dimensions

teacher_modes.shared_rotated_lora: all task deltas are A R(theta_i) B for shared A,B
teacher_modes.independent_lora: eight unrelated rank-2 A_i B_i updates

controls: one shared rank-2 LoRA for every task
two generic shared rank-2 LoRA bases with learned per-task coefficients
small task-embedding hypernetwork that emits two shared-basis coefficients
shared rank-2 LoRA with one Mirror angle per task

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE pooled across methods and teacher modes

training.task_address: oracle task id; no learned routing

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference payload bytes
storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: In all three fresh shared-rotated-Lora worlds, Mirror MSE <=1.10x independent LoRA-bank MSE and actual payload <=0.40x LoRA bank; it must beat generic shared-basis/hypernetwork controls by >=10% in bytes at <=5% MSE cost. Independent mode is a private-capacity boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses full-LoRA quality/storage in at least two fresh worlds or a simpler shared-basis/hypernetwork control matches quality with equal/lower payload and compute. Independent-mode failure alone is a structural boundary.
boundaries: linear adapter deltas over frozen features only
teacher deliberately aligned to rank-space rotation
oracle task IDs, no routing claim
fixed-update synthetic screen, no language/capacity claim
